You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 356b57752c91cffb35356abe6647065bf0edcad1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Feb 2018 12:10:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
---
 drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
index d1a01311c1a2..5e3df194723e 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
@@ -376,6 +376,7 @@ static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the failure to reset the wakeup capable flag for the intel-hid device upon its removal. This oversight meant that even after the device was removed and its notify handler was no longer active, the system still incorrectly believed that the device could wake it up from suspend-to-idle, leading to potential unexpected behavior. The patch corrects this by explicitly setting the wakeup capability to false during the device removal process.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the failure to reset the wakeup capable flag for the intel-hid device upon its removal. This oversight meant that even after the device was removed and its notify handler was no longer active, the system still incorrectly believed that the device could wake it up from suspend-to-idle, leading to potential unexpected behavior. The patch corrects this by explicitly setting the wakeup capability to false during the device removal process.
